options.title: How Did Motorola Build the First Mobile Phone?
options.first_line: How did Motorola build a phone you could carry down the street, when nobody ever had?
options.first_frame: A chunky beige 1970s handset spins up out of the dark, its shell splitting open to show the glowing radio boards inside, with the word MOTOROLA on its side.

options.title: Motorola Had 6 Weeks to Invent the Mobile Phone
options.first_line: Motorola had six weeks to build something nobody had ever made: a phone you could carry.
options.first_frame: A wall calendar flips its pages fast in a dark workshop while a brick-sized handset assembles itself on the bench in front of it.

options.title: Why Was the First Mobile Phone a Brick?
options.first_line: The first mobile phone you could carry was Motorola's, and it was the size of a brick. Why?
options.first_frame: A huge 1973 Motorola handset stands next to a modern phone at true size on a lit stage, the old one towering over it.

why: It names Motorola and the phone in your own pocket, the first frame shows the towering brick next to a modern phone even with the sound off, and it asks why without giving the answer, while B spends a figure in the title and A's question is vaguer to picture.
